DILG Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 136 s. 2022 October 20, 2022 ATTY. PASTOR C. LIGAS, JR. Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Rizal Province of Cagayan Dear Atty. Ligas, Jr.: This has reference to your letter dated IO September 2022 requesting for this Department's legal opinion on the following: iv. V. Who must accept the resignation of the IPMR to become effective? If the resignation letter of the IPMR was never presented before as open session of the sanggunian, will the submission alone of the letter to the Office of the Sangguniang Bayan enough to consider the said member as resigned? Is it enough that only the Presiding Officer (Vice-Mayor) alone shall accept the said resignation of the IPMR? What is the effect if there was no proper acceptance of the resignation letter of the IPMR by the appropriate officer or body? Is the vacancy capable of being filled up by appointment by the Local Chief Executive considering that the term of the resigned IPMR in the sanggunian still has two (2) more years left? Per your letter, Hon. Glefiver Ruma Rivera, IPMR in the Sangguniang Bayan of the Municipality of Rizal, Cagayan tendered his resignation letter to then Vice-Mayor, Atty. Joel A. Ruma last May 2022, and then stopped attending the sessions of the sanggunian thereafter. You contended that while Section 82 of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides for the resignation of elective local officials to become effective only by the acceptance of the sanggunian concerned, the same Code did not provide for the acceptance and effectivity of a member of the sanggunian whose membership therein was not derived through election. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Thus, the above specified queries. Foremost, in Legal Opinion No. 13, s. 2014, the Department has already settled that the position of IPMR is necessarily elective in nature, thus: "2. This Department has been consistent on its opinion that it is not the mode to which one acquired office that determines the nature and character of such office. It is the function or role of said that is controlling. Our classic example is the case of two(2) incumbent regular sanggunian members who were appointed therein to fill the permanent vacancies in the aforesaid August Body. While it may be true that they acquired their positions thru appointment, they should not be considered as appointive members of the sanggunian. The nature and character of the office of the regular member of the sanggunian is elective, the assumption to which, while generally determined by an election, is not precluded by appointment to fill the permanent vacancies that may arise therein. RA 8371 mandates the representation of ICCs/lPs in the local sanggunians at all levels. Such IP/ICC representatives shall represent the ICCs/lPs at all levels of decision-making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through procedures determined by them and in doing so, the ICC/IP representative • necessarily will propose in the local sanggunian legislative measures (i.e. ordinance/resolution) towards developing ICC/IP conditions and particpate in the deliberations thereof In fact, in DILG Opinion No. 2Q series of 2011, the ICC/IP representative was referred as "ef-officio meber of the local sanggunian", the same term that we use to refer to the president of the liga ng mga barangay and sangguniang kabataan from municipal to provincial levels; 3. Lastly, Section 6, Rule IV of the Implementing Rules and Regulations ofRA 8371 as reiterated under Section 13 of NCIP AO No. 001, series of 2009, categorically states that ICC/IP representatives shall have the same compensation. benefits, and other emoluments as th ular members of the le islative bodies and/or Olic makinq bodies". In view thereof, Section 82 of the LGC can be applied in the instant case, thus: "SECTION 82. Resignation of Elective Local Officials — (a) Resignations by elective local officials shall be deemed effective only upon acceptance by the following authorities: xxx xxx xxx (3) The Sanggunian concerned, in the case of Sanggunian members; and (4) The city or municipal mayor, in the case of barangay officials. (b) Copies of the resignation letters of elective local officials, together with the action taken by the aforesaid authorities, shall be furnished the Department of the Interior and Local Government. (c) The resignation shall be deemed accepted if not acted upon by the authority concemed within fifteen (15) working days from receipt thereof. Page 2 of 3

(d) Inevocable resignations by sanggunian members shall be deemed accepted upon presentation before an open session of the sanggunian concerned and duly entered in its records: Provided, however, That this subsection does not apply to sanggunian members who are subject to recall elections or to cases where existing laws prescribe the manner of acting upon such resignations. Accordingly, a member of the sanggunian may resign through (I) resignation letter and such resignation shall be effective only upon acceptance by the sanggunian concerned or such is deemed accepted if not acted upon by the same sanggunian within 15 days from receipt thereof; and (2) Irrevocable resignation by sanggunian member shall be deemed accepted upon presentation before an open session of the sanggunian concerned and duly entered in its records. With respect to the last concern, we answer in the negative. The vacancy created is not capable of being filled up by appointment by the Local Chief Executive. In this case, Administrative Order No. 03, S.20181 should be applied, Section 24 of which reads: "Section 21. Vacancy. A permanent vacancy which occurs by reason Of death, incapacity, removal or resignation, shall be filled up in accordance with the local guidelines. The successor shall serve the unexpired term. However, if the unexpired term is less than six months, the concemed ICCs/lPs shall instead select a successor for a full term of office. The IPMR selected shall have the same powers, duties and functions as well as entitlements and privileges accorded to the predecessor. " Be that as it is, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY A O ITY OF THE SECRETARY: VICTOR R. LLAMAS etary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs Unde OUSE JVULLLS-LRALLD/rrao copy furnish: DIR. JONATHAN PAUL M.
